problem: Machine-learning interatomic potentials struggle to accurately capture long-range interactions in large molecular systems like biomolecules and electrolytes.
approach: AllScAIP uses an all-to-all node attention component in an energy-conserving architecture to capture long-range interactions in a purely data-driven manner, scaling to 100 million training samples.
contribution: The model achieves state-of-the-art energy/force accuracy on molecular systems (OMol25) and enables stable, long-timescale MD simulations that recover experimental observables.

problem: Flow-based policies in RL offer high expressivity but naive gradient-based optimization is unstable due to backpropagation through numerical solvers.
approach: Q-Flow propagates terminal value to intermediate latent states along the flow trajectory, enabling stable policy optimization using intermediate value gradients without unrolling the solver.
contribution: Q-Flow outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on OGBench by an average of 10.6 percentage points in offline learning while maintaining stability for online adaptation.

problem: Generative tabular augmentation prioritizes distributional fidelity but fails to reliably improve downstream model performance due to a fidelity-utility gap.
approach: TAP couples diffusion inpainting with a learner-conditioned policy to steer generation toward high-utility regions and controls injection timing via gating and conservative commitment.
contribution: Under severe data scarcity, TAP improves classification accuracy by up to 15.6 percentage points and reduces regression RMSE by up to 32% compared to strong generative baselines.

problem: Structure-based drug design typically conditions on empty pockets, missing informative components like fillers and solvent that capture binding environment properties.
approach: EDMolGPT uses low-resolution electron density derived from fillers as a physically grounded condition for de novo drug design, supporting both computational and experimental sources via unified pre-training.
contribution: The method produces molecules with 3D conformations and demonstrates effectiveness on 101 biological targets.

problem: Single-teacher semi-supervised learning relies on categorical pseudo-labels without perceiving loss geometry, leading to unstable optimization and limited generalization.
approach: TTN integrates complementary supervision from MAE and DINOv3, fusing their pseudo-labels and local Hessians via confidence weighting, then updates student parameters preconditioned by the fused curvature.
contribution: TTN consistently improves over single-teacher and consistency-based methods on ImageNet, CIFAR-10, SVHN, and STL-10.

problem: Behavior cloning often fails with limited expert demonstrations in offline imitation learning.
approach: PIDM combines a future state predictor with an inverse dynamics model; predicting future state introduces bias but conditioning the IDM on prediction reduces variance.
contribution: PIDM achieves lower prediction error and requires up to five times fewer demonstrations than BC on 2D navigation; on complex 3D environments, BC requires over 66% more samples than PIDM.

problem: Deep neural networks for image classification are overconfident on out-of-distribution samples.
approach: GCOS synthesizes virtual outliers in hidden feature space respecting the learned manifold structure via a dominant-variance subspace and conformally-inspired shell, combined with contrastive regularization.
contribution: GCOS outperforms state-of-the-art methods using energy-based inference on near-OOD benchmarks and naturally extends to conformal OOD inference.

problem: Learning reliable goal-conditioned value functions in long-horizon offline tasks remains challenging due to erroneous generalization.
approach: LAVL integrates latent-representation-based value generalization with hierarchical planning, using structured representations to improve value function reliability.
contribution: LAVL achieves highest performance on 20 out of 22 OGBench datasets and exhibits strong performance on long-horizon and trajectory stitching tasks.

problem: KL-entropy-regularized RL methods do not outperform entropy-only methods in continuous action domains despite theoretical guarantees.
approach: MDAC instantiates Mirror Descent Value Iteration for continuous actions in actor-critic style and boosts performance by bounding the actor's log-probability in the critic's loss.
contribution: MDAC performs better than non-regularized and entropy-only methods with appropriate choice of bounding functions.

problem: In overparametrized neural networks, parameter non-identifiability causes substantial parameter uncertainty to persist even when the underlying function is fully identified.
approach: The work analyzes epistemic uncertainty through non-identifiability, characterizing both discrete and continuous sources of residual uncertainty in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
contribution: The analysis provides theoretical insights into posterior structure and validates findings through empirical studies on ReLU networks.

problem: Static pattern-based bug detectors fail to generalize beyond predefined templates and struggle to find Recurring Pattern Bugs that appear across multiple code segments.
approach: BugStone combines LLVM-based program analysis with LLMs to synthesize abstract error patterns from a single patched instance and retrieve semantically similar bugs throughout the codebase.
contribution: On a ground truth dataset of 1.9K security bugs, BugStone achieves 92.2% precision and 79.1% pairwise accuracy; in the Linux kernel, it identified over 22K potential issues with manual audit confirming 246 valid bugs.

problem: Universal approximation of permutation-invariant functions requires a latent dimension scaling as O(N), creating a scalability bottleneck for set-based architectures.
approach: For Wasserstein-stable functions, the work derives a multiscale Random Fourier Feature encoder and McShane-extended Hölder decoder to prove that O(log N) latent dimension suffices.
contribution: The constructive bound for O(log N) latent dimension is an exponential improvement over prior O(N) requirements.

problem: Laboratory robotic tasks require trajectory-level safety throughout execution, yet most robot benchmarks evaluate reversible tasks and imitation policies lack recovery signals.
approach: SafeLab couples a verified generative simulation engine with an automated teleoperation-free expert and safety-aware RL, featuring 63 calibrated lab assets and 6,400 expert trajectories.
contribution: SafeLab reveals unsafe-but-successful trajectories and bounded residual RL improves simulated Safe Success Rate by up to 43 percentage points; physical replays show 86% agreement between simulation and observed safety.

problem: Object insertion for remote sensing augmentation suffers from semantic placement inconsistency, radiometric inconsistency, and textural discontinuity.
approach: PDA uses a Planning module for geometric validity, a Decoupling module for spectral adaptation to disentangle identity from illumination, and an Assimilation module for texture harmonization.
contribution: PDA reduces whole-image FID by 15.7% over the strongest baseline and boosts downstream detection mAP50 by +17.07 points over real data.

problem: Standard GNN aggregation functions like mean, max, and sum are not invertible, limiting applicability to tasks requiring invertible transformations.
approach: InvGNN introduces an invertible GNN layer that stacks to form fully invertible models, inheriting benefits of invertible neural networks including low memory, exact likelihood computation, and generative capabilities.
contribution: InvGNNs match the expressive power of the 1-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm and perform comparably to established GNNs on classification while enabling density estimation and node feature generation.

problem: Determining geographic location from audio signals remains unexplored, particularly for wildlife and natural sounds.
approach: The work benchmarks image geolocation and soundscape methods, proposes a hybrid approach combining species range prediction with retrieval-based geolocation, and explores multimodal geolocation with audio-visual content.
contribution: Results highlight the potential of incorporating bioacoustic signals into geospatial tasks.

problem: Gradient estimation for stochastic differentiable relaxations of non-differentiable functions typically requires differentiable densities with full support, limiting flexibility.
approach: The work derives stochastic smoothing with reduced assumptions without requiring differentiable density or full support, developing variance reduction from three orthogonal perspectives.
contribution: Empirical benchmarking of 6 distributions and up to 24 variance reduction strategies for differentiable sorting, ranking, shortest-paths, rendering, and cryo-electron tomography.

problem: Standard Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures remain deterministic with limited uncertainty estimates for planning and control.
approach: VJEPA learns predictive distributions over future latent states via a latent-space variational objective; BJEPA combines dynamics experts with modular priors through Product of Experts for constraint-aware prediction.
contribution: VJEPA-family objectives are more robust to high-variance distractors than reconstruction-based baselines on Noisy-TV, nonlinear, and image-based benchmarks.

problem: LLM agents typically invoke tools one at a time without global task structure awareness, leading to error accumulation when scaling to hundreds or thousands of tools.
approach: NaviAgent uses a bilevel architecture decoupling task planning from tool execution via graph-based modeling of tool relations and a Tool World Navigation Model encoding structural relations.
contribution: NaviAgent achieves consistent improvements in task success rate with TWNM yielding an average gain of 13.1 points on complex tasks and 4.3-12.0 points on real APIs.

problem: Temporal Difference learning in average-reward settings faces theoretical difficulties because the Bellman operator is not contractive, complicating convergence analysis.
approach: The work introduces an algorithm sampling from two Markovian trajectories for average-reward policy evaluation, guaranteeing convergence to the unique solution of a properly defined projected Bellman equation.
contribution: The convergence analysis is uniformly applicable to both linear function approximation and tabular settings without explicit dimension-dependent terms, achieving quadratic sample complexity improvement over prior quartic scaling.

problem: Existing ADMM analyses for multiblock problems with block anti-upper triangular constraints rely on restrictive assumptions about the entire constraint matrix.
approach: The work proposes a new assumption to guarantee convergence of proximal ADMM for nonconvex problems with block anti-upper triangular constraints.
contribution: Extends theoretical understanding of multi-block ADMM and proves linear convergence under four different scenarios in the strongly convex setting.

problem: Existing diffusion-based dataset distillation relies on per-sample update rules that evolve synthetic images independently, limiting optimization of collective set-level objectives.
approach: SCG injects set-symmetric feedback at each diffusion step via spectral set-point regulation and cooperative kernel coupling, operating on lightweight descriptors from predicted clean latents.
contribution: Consistent accuracy gains across multiple diffusion-based baselines on ImageNette, ImageWoof, ImageNet-100, and ImageNet-1K.

problem: Predicting transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations typically assumes gene-independence but responses manifest as coordinated program-level changes among functionally related genes.
approach: scBIG induces coherent gene programs via Gene-Relation Clustering, captures inter-program interactions through a Gene-Cluster-Aware Encoder, and preserves modular coordination using conditional flow matching.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods with an average improvement of 6.7%, particularly on unseen and combinatorial perturbation settings.

problem: Standard MCTS methods like AlphaZero's MCTS-UCB require extensive simulations to achieve high-quality action values.
approach: RMCTS recursively re-estimates action values using regularized optimal posterior policies from MCTS as regularized policy optimization at each node, starting from leaves and working back to root.
contribution: RMCTS matches or exceeds AlphaZero's MCTS-UCB quality in a tiny fraction of the time.

problem: Multi-LoRA agent systems incur substantial memory and compute overhead by building independent KV caches for identical long tool-augmented trajectories.
approach: LRAgent decomposes cache into shared base component from pretrained weights and adapter-dependent component from LoRA, further reducing compute via shared-A multi-LoRA architectures.
contribution: Achieves throughput and latency close to fully shared caching while preserving accuracy near non-shared baseline across agentic question-answering.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models relying on explicit Chain-of-Thought reasoning suffer from high computational costs and error propagation in multi-step tasks.
approach: AVA-VLA models reasoning as unobservable latent variables, uses RL-based denoising to optimize reasoning trajectories via task rewards, and incorporates early-exit strategy for adaptive efficiency.
contribution: Significantly reduces inference latency while achieving superior stability and success rates compared to full-reasoning baselines.

problem: Theories of deep Transformers predict token collapse to a single point but fail to account for deterministic weight initialization noise.
approach: The work analyzes deep Transformers with noise from random initialization, showing tokens converge to an interacting-particle system where common matrix-valued Brownian noise drives dynamics.
contribution: Proves initialization noise prevents collapse predicted by deterministic models and reveals phase transitions with antipodal configurations becoming attracting with positive probability.

problem: 6D pose estimation and tracking remain brittle, relying on CAD models and manual masking, failing under occlusion or fast motion without recognizing failure.
approach: STORM combines Hierarchical Spatial Fusion Attention supporting single/multi-reference conditioning with a BCE-trained tracking verifier whose compatibility logit detects drift and triggers automatic re-initialization.
contribution: Improves annotation-free pose tracking and reliably recovers from severe occlusions and viewpoint changes on LM-O and YCB-Video.

problem: Existing variance concentration inequalities for bounded random variables require restrictive assumptions and are not sharp for sequential decision making.
approach: The work develops empirical Bernstein inequalities holding under constant conditional variance and mean without independence or identical distribution, for both batch and sequential settings.
contribution: Bounds are asymptotically sharp when data are iid, adapting optimally to both unknown mean and unknown variance, and extend to separable Hilbert spaces.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts model compression via expert-level pruning is too coarse and misallocates budgets since information is concentrated in few channels even in high-importance experts.
approach: Proposes structural pruning reforming prune-ratio objective to maximize channel-score coverage via efficient attribution-based approximation.
contribution: Retains accuracy under 50% or 25% pruning with 4-bit quantization, reducing Qwen3-30B-A3B memory footprint by 5.27x.

problem: Directly optimizing answer-level objectives in language models is computationally intractable due to marginalizing over vast latent reasoning paths.
approach: Formulates answer-level fine-tuning as a Distributional Alignment Game between a Policy and auxiliary Target distribution, proving Nash Equilibrium corresponds to the original optimization problem.
contribution: Transforms intractable marginalization into tractable projection and unifies diversity and self-improvement approaches with efficient algorithms compatible with GRPO.

problem: Theoretical understanding of out-of-distribution performance in conditional flow matching remains limited.
approach: Treats conditional task as a map from condition space to Wasserstein space, deriving generalization bound under coarse embedding assumption and decomposing OOD error into Interpolation Sparsity, Geometric Distortion, and In-Distribution Fit.
contribution: Framework acts as diagnostic tool tracking generalization during training and identifies dataset-specific failure modes.

problem: Standard-cell characterization relies on slow simulation sweeps and many fast predictors ignore layout geometry, missing coupling and layout-dependent effects.
approach: FusionCell treats routed layout geometry and netlist topology as dual-modality inputs fused via topology-guided mechanism where netlist acts as structural map querying layout regions.
contribution: Reduces regression error (average MAPE 0.92%) and improves ranking over baselines while accelerating characterization by orders of magnitude.

problem: Vision Transformers fail at spatial reasoning tasks like mental rotation, often attributed to data scale but potentially stemming from architecture limits.
approach: Formalizes spatial understanding as a Group Homomorphism Problem and identifies fundamental bottleneck via complexity theory: non-solvable groups like SO(3) require NC1-complete Word Problem computation.
contribution: Proves constant-depth ViTs with polynomial precision are bounded by TC0, creating complexity boundary preventing capture of non-solvable spatial structures.

problem: Hybridizing mechanistic epidemiological models with neural models often fails under partial observability and non-stationary transmission dynamics.
approach: Decomposes infections into trend, seasonal, and residual components using these as control signals for a controlled neural ODE coupled to epidemiological model.
contribution: Attains lowest RMSE on all five datasets (up to 57% reduction), predicts peak within one time step on four of five, and recovers time-varying rates without auxiliary covariates.

problem: Model attribution from discrete diffusion LLM responses is challenging due to diverse attribution scenarios and redundant confidence signals.
approach: Proposes Directed Decoding Map extracting structural relationships between decoding steps and Gaussian-Trajectory Attribution fitting cell-wise distributions per model.
contribution: Enables effective model identification across scenarios including distinguishing different models, checkpoints, and backups.

problem: Tabular foundation models like TabPFN are competitive but improve with increasingly complex architectures, incurring higher inference cost and limiting deployment.
approach: TabSwift revisits TabPFN design showing row-wise attention backbone remains competitive with gated attention stabilization and learnable register tokens, plus adaptive early-exit mechanism.
contribution: Competitive with stronger models like TabPFN v2 and TabICL while being more efficient; supports anytime inference via layer-wise early-exit.

problem: Existing document parsing benchmarks focus on high-resource languages, creating evaluation gaps for model performance on diverse languages and structural complexity.
approach: MORE covers 149 languages with structural complexity beyond plain text including code blocks, tables, and catalogs, with authentic data via model-assisted human-refined annotation.
contribution: Establishes new performance baselines for long-tail languages and validates benchmark effectiveness in diagnosing model capabilities on realistic scenarios.

problem: Existing LLM watermark detection methods focus on offline settings and fail to control online False Discovery Rate when applied to streams mixing machine-generated and human text.
approach: LORD-GoF combines Goodness-of-Fit statistic with Levels based On Recent Discovery procedure, dynamically adjusting detection thresholds to rigorously control oFDR.
contribution: Maintains statistical power comparable to offline benchmarks while controlling oFDR under complex mixed streaming scenarios.

problem: Chain-of-Thought reasoning in LLMs incurs long natural-language rationales poorly aligned with efficient machine reasoning.
approach: CLSR enables agents to autonomously invent, evolve, and share compact Language Symbolism Frameworks while an adaptive router selects and composes languages to optimize accuracy-token trade-off.
contribution: Reduces latency-oriented token completion by 3-6x compared to standard CoT while maintaining accuracy.
